text.title: AI Prompt as Commit Artefact Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules governing the Faion-* git trailer block that records prompt, model and verification for an AI-assisted commit. Each rule is checkable against `git interpret-trailers --parse` output, the hook file, or the commit message itself.

rule.statement: The `Faion-Prompt` / `Faion-Model` / `Faion-Context` / `Faion-Verifier` lines MUST form the last paragraph of the commit message — one `Token: value` per line, no blank line inside the block, no prose after it. Check: `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Faion-Model,valueonly)'` returns a non-empty value.

rationale.source: git-interpret-trailers(1), "the trailer block is the last non-whitespace-only paragraph"

rule.rationale: Git's trailer parser only scans the final paragraph. A blank line or a trailing sentence after the block makes `%(trailers:...)` expand to the empty string, so every audit query silently reports zero AI-assisted commits while the text is still visibly there in `git show`.

rule.statement: Enforcement lives in `.git/hooks/commit-msg` (or the `commit-msg` stage of a pre-commit framework), which receives the message file path as `$1` and validates it with `git interpret-trailers --parse`. A `pre-commit`-stage hook MUST NOT be used for this check.

rationale.source: githooks(5) — hook invocation order and arguments

rule.rationale: The `pre-commit` hook runs before the message exists and is passed no message argument, so a trailer check placed there can only ever inspect the previous commit or nothing at all — it passes unconditionally and the gate is decorative.

rule.statement: `Faion-Model` MUST record the fully-resolved model identifier including its dated or versioned suffix (e.g. `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`). Moving aliases (`-latest`, `default`, a bare product name, an IDE brand name like "Copilot") are rejected by the hook.

rationale.source: Anthropic / OpenAI model-deprecation and alias policy

rule.rationale: Aliases are repointed to a newer snapshot on the vendor's schedule. A trailer that says `latest` names a different model every month, so the reproduction attempt six months later re-runs a model that never produced this diff and the disagreement is unattributable.

rule.statement: A prompt longer than one line MUST be committed as a file in the same commit (convention: `.prompts/<short-sha-or-slug>.md`) with the trailer carrying the path plus a digest — `Faion-Prompt: .prompts/checkout-retry.md sha256:9f2a…`. Verbatim multi-paragraph prompts in the trailer value are rejected.
rule.rationale: A trailer value is one logical line; continuation requires every wrapped line to start with whitespace, and a prompt containing a blank line or a line beginning with `#` or `-` terminates or corrupts the block. The digest is what makes the reference falsifiable — a later edit to the prompt file no longer matches the commit.

rule.statement: Prompt text and `Faion-Context` values MUST be scrubbed of credentials, tokens, customer records and PII before they enter the message; the hook runs a secret scanner (gitleaks, detect-secrets, `git secrets`) over the message body, not only over the diff.
rule.rationale: Message text is part of the commit object and is covered by the object's SHA. Removing it requires rewriting every descendant commit and force-pushing, and any fork, CI cache or mirror that already fetched the object keeps the secret — so the only cheap moment is before the commit is created.

rule.statement: When the forge squash-merges, the squash commit message MUST be regenerated to hold exactly one Faion-* block. Check: `git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Faion-Model,valueonly)' | wc -l` equals 1 on the merged commit.
rule.rationale: Squash concatenates the branch's commit messages, so a five-commit branch yields five `Faion-Model` lines in one message. `valueonly` then returns all of them and any consumer that reads the first value attributes the whole diff to whichever model happened to touch the first commit.

rule.statement: Do NOT apply when (a) the commit contains no AI-authored hunk — pure formatter output, generated lockfile, `git revert`; (b) the branch is a throwaway prototype that will be deleted rather than merged; (c) the repository forbids extra trailers because a downstream tool parses the message strictly (release-please, commitlint with a closed trailer allowlist) and the allowlist has not been extended.
rule.rationale: A trailer on a non-AI commit is a false positive that inflates the audit denominator; a trailer a strict parser does not know about fails the release job, so the tool config must be extended before the discipline is turned on.
